scope: Characterize FUN_004E20A0 - the Map tick handler that is the sole caller of the s2c packet dispatcher FUN_004DC690. Determine what state is mutated per tick beyond packet dispatch, identify the call-tree position, and trace whether the actor map at zone+0x17804..+0x17808 is iterated here or by a sibling helper. Resolve whether Actor cluster opcodes (the 24 multi-case fallthrough opcodes the actor-cluster-dispatch-model pass mapped to actor->vftable[9]) get their effects applied somewhere other than the (no-op per the actor-vtable9-bulk pass) vftable[9] slot.

method.step1: Re-decomped FUN_004E20A0 (1442 body bytes) plus 12 of its uncataloged direct callees (FUN_004E5FF0, FUN_004E12F0, FUN_004D0760, FUN_00DB7110, FUN_00DB7130, FUN_004E3EB0, FUN_004DA670, FUN_00DB70F0, FUN_004E38B0, FUN_004E4270, FUN_00DADF50, plus the immediate caller FUN_004E30A0 (837 body bytes)). Output: ghidra-projects/fun_004e20a0_decomp.txt.
method.step2: Re-used existing decomps for callees decompiled in prior phases: FUN_004DC690, FUN_004B3C50 (parent of FUN_004E30A0), FUN_004DAA10 (the sibling helper called by FUN_004B3C50 immediately before FUN_004E30A0), FUN_004DDB50 (the lock-free queue dequeue primitive), FUN_00DAE3B0 / FUN_00DAE1E0 (Zone connection-manager getter + 0x02 handshake emitter), FUN_004D9910 / BCS-Y-0534 (zone+0x17804..+0x17808 actor-map find primitive).
method.step3: Cross-referenced every callee against manifests/symbols.json by name + by VA (case-insensitive both ways since some catalog entries have a known 0x000XXXXX vs 0x004XXXXX leading-digit typo). Identified 4 callees with prior catalog entries (FUN_004DC690/BCS-Y-0279, FUN_00DAE010/BCS-Y-0304, FUN_004E0240/BCS-Y-0312 via thunk_FUN_004E0240, FUN_00DAE520/BCS-Y-0107) and the function itself (FUN_004E20A0/BCS-Y-0314); ALL other direct callees are uncataloged.
method.step4: Traced the call tree upward from FUN_004E20A0: -> FUN_004E30A0 (uncataloged 837-byte state-machine pump) -> FUN_004B3C50 (uncataloged 523-byte per-frame Scene+Map tick that ALSO calls the per-tick actor-event drain FUN_004DAA10 and the ScenePacket builder FUN_004EC080). FUN_004B3C50 has NO callers in static xref - it is the top of the chain that the project's frame-loop / scheduler invokes by function pointer.
method.step5: Re-read FUN_004DAA10 from its existing decomp - confirmed it is a PRODUCER-CONSUMER LOCK-FREE LOOP draining a ring buffer via FUN_004DDB50, and for each entry it looks up the actor via FUN_004D9910 (BCS-Y-0534, the zone+0x17804..+0x17808 actor-map find) then dispatches to actor->vtable[8] (offset 0x20) with (event_type-3, payload_ptr+0x20, payload_word+0x18). This is the per-tick per-actor effect application path that BYPASSES vtable[9] entirely.

function_metadata.name: ZoneOutbound_TickHandler_FUN_004E20A0
function_metadata.primary_purpose_refined: Per-frame Map channel pump invoked from FUN_004E30A0 case 4 (running state) and case 5 (shutdown drain). NOT an actor iterator. Two responsibilities: (a) DRAIN INBOUND PACKET QUEUE - a while loop that calls FUN_00DAE520 to dequeue the next s2c packet from the Map channel's inbox at param_1+0x234, normalizes the opcode via 0x5ff80000 mask, then hands the packet to FUN_004DC690 (the s2c central dispatcher); per packet it also runs a state-machine switch on the packet opcode (cases 1/2/0xE/0x11) that may emit response c2s opcodes (0x04, 0x06) or schedule timing updates; (b) EMIT PERIODIC C2S 0x01 PING - gated on idle (no inbound progress) and a per-second time tick (__time64 mod compare), emits c2s opcode 1 size 0x28 via thunk_FUN_004E0240 (BCS-Y-0312) and updates bandwidth stats (FUN_00DB70F0/FUN_00DB7110 byte counters scaled by FUN_009DA820 fpoint math into param_1+0x380/+0x384).

tick_structure.actor_map_iteration_in_function: NO - FUN_004E20A0 does NOT iterate zone+0x17804..+0x17808 itself. The actor-map iteration happens in a SIBLING function FUN_004DAA10 that the same parent (FUN_004B3C50) calls earlier in the per-frame tick, BEFORE invoking FUN_004E30A0 -> FUN_004E20A0.
tick_structure.sibling_actor_iteration_pattern: Producer-consumer drain: while(entry = FUN_004DDB50(&slot)) { if (entry.type==2) sound/animation channel call on zone+0x17924->vtable[6]; else { actor = FUN_004D9910(entry.actor_id); if (actor) actor->vtable[8](entry.type-3, entry.payload+0x20, entry.payload+0x18); } InterlockedDecrement(zone+0x17938 if ring slot ready); }
tick_structure.sibling_actor_iteration_vtable_slot: actor->vtable[8] (offset 0x20), NOT vtable[9] (offset 0x24). vtable[8] takes 3 args (event_type subtracted by 3, payload_ptr, extra_word) and IS the polymorphic per-actor-class state-application slot. The actor-vtable9-bulk pass found vtable[9] is no-op; the real apply slot for the per-tick actor-event drain is vtable[8].
tick_structure.packet_dispatch_call_site: Decomp line 152: FUN_004dc690(uVar5, uVar8) where uVar5 = opcode (post-mask) and uVar8 = packet body pointer at local_1178+0x24. Inside a while loop that repeats while FUN_00DAE520 returns non-zero (queue still has packets).
tick_structure.packet_queue_field: param_1 + 0x234 (Map channel state inbox); the queue node iterator is local_1178; the packet body is at *(local_1178 + 0x24).

key_findings.title: FUN_004E20A0 does NOT iterate the actor map - it is a packet-queue drain, not an actor pump
key_findings.detail: Empirically confirmed by reading the 1442-byte body: the only iteration is a while loop calling FUN_00DAE520 (BCS-Y-0107, zone connection state machine dispatch frame) which pops s2c packets off param_1+0x234. There is no read of zone+0x17804 / zone+0x17808 anywhere in the function. The actor-cluster-dispatch-model pass's hypothesis ('FUN_004E20A0 Map tick handler') was correct in name but the verb was overloaded - it's a CHANNEL tick (packets in, periodic c2s out), not an ACTOR tick.
key_findings.implication: The actor-vtable9-bulk pass finding that vftable[9] on actor classes is no-op is consistent with this discovery. Actor-cluster opcode handlers (cases 0x0F / 0xCC..0xE5 in FUN_004DC690) DO call actor->vftable[9] but those are no-ops; the actual per-actor effects happen elsewhere. The per-frame caller chain has an actor-event drain (FUN_004DAA10) at the level ABOVE FUN_004E20A0, not below.

key_findings.title: FUN_004DAA10 is the per-tick actor pump and uses vtable[8], NOT vtable[9]
key_findings.detail: FUN_004DAA10 (310 bytes, sole caller FUN_004B3C50) drains a lock-free ring buffer via FUN_004DDB50 producer-consumer queue (Interlocked* primitives, 0x60-byte entries). For each entry it (a) classifies by entry.type at +0x14: type==2 is a special sound/animation-channel call on zone+0x17924->vtable[6]; otherwise (b) looks up actor via FUN_004D9910(entry.actor_id at +0x10) (BCS-Y-0534) then invokes actor->vtable[8] (offset 0x20) with (event_type-3, payload_ptr+0x20, payload+0x18). The 3-arg actor->vtable[8] call is the polymorphic per-actor-class apply slot. The vtable[9] survey found no-op implementations across actor classes; an equivalent vtable[8] survey would test this attribution.
key_findings.implication: Actor cluster opcode EFFECTS are applied via the **producer-consumer queue + actor->vtable[8] pattern** in FUN_004DAA10, not via reactive packet handlers in FUN_004DC690's vtable[9] dispatch. The QUEUE PRODUCER side is the missing link - somewhere a write path enqueues an actor event when an Actor cluster s2c packet arrives. Candidate enqueue sites: FUN_004DC690 case 0x0F/0xCC..0xE5 (the multi-case fallthrough that invokes vftable[9] - the no-op vftable[9] call may be a LEFTOVER and the REAL enqueue happens before it via case-specific code that's collapsed in decomp), or FUN_004DA670/FUN_004DA380 (called from FUN_004E20A0's shutdown path - probably wrong direction), or in unrelated network-receive paths.

key_findings.title: The tick chain has FOUR levels - not all are pumps; some are pure state-build
key_findings.detail: FUN_004B3C50 (top, per-frame Scene+Map tick) -> FUN_004E30A0 (state-machine pump) -> FUN_004E20A0 (channel packet pump) -> FUN_004DC690 (s2c dispatcher). FUN_004B3C50 additionally calls FUN_004DAA10 (actor-event drain) and FUN_004EC080 (ScenePacket builder) at the same level as FUN_004E30A0 - they all run once per frame in fixed order: stash sub-object iterator state -> drain actor events -> build ScenePacket -> drive Map channel state machine -> dispatch ScenePacket. FUN_004B3C50 has NO STATIC CALLERS in xref - it is invoked by function pointer from the outer frame loop (TBD - candidate is the main GameLoop or the Engine::FrameTick scheduler).
key_findings.implication: The 'Map tick' label is overloaded in three senses: (1) FUN_004B3C50 is the per-frame composite tick; (2) FUN_004E30A0 is the per-frame Map channel state-machine pump; (3) FUN_004E20A0 is the per-frame Map channel packet pump. Each does a different job. Catalog entries should distinguish by name suffix.

key_findings.title: Periodic c2s emissions from the tick handler total FOUR distinct opcodes
key_findings.detail: (1) c2s 0x01 size 0x28 - the per-second heartbeat ping (post-loop time-tick branch); (2) c2s 0x04 size 0x18 - the zone-leave / shutdown response (per-packet switch cases 0xE/0x11); (3) c2s 0x06 size 0x18 - the case-2 response (per-packet switch case 2); (4) c2s 0xCA UpdatePlayerPositionPacket via FUN_004DC690 case 7 (one level deeper but same call chain). All four are already cataloged at the EMIT site (BCS-Y-0314 covers 1/2/3; BCS-Y-0321 covers 4); no new outbound opcode bindings emerge here.
key_findings.implication: The tick handler is BOTH a sink (drains inbound s2c) AND a source (emits periodic c2s). The opcode catalogue already documents this fully. What's NEW here is the call-tree position and the actor-pump sibling identification.

key_findings.title: NO Lua _onLoop hook in the FUN_004E20A0 tick handler itself
key_findings.detail: Static scan of FUN_004E20A0's direct callees finds no reference to FUN_00CC7A90 (Lua dispatcher per BCS-Y-0311), FUN_00447260 (std::string builder commonly used for Lua API name lookup), or any of the known LuaActorImpl wrapper VAs from prior phases. The Map subsystem does NOT fire Lua _onLoop callbacks per tick at this level. If a Lua _onLoop hook exists, it must be one of: (a) inside actor->vtable[8] implementations (called by FUN_004DAA10) where individual actor classes may dispatch to Lua; (b) inside FUN_00C99830 / FUN_00C98160 / FUN_00C97030 (the unknown engine helpers called by FUN_004B3C50 before FUN_004E30A0); (c) at the outer frame-loop level (above FUN_004B3C50).
key_findings.implication: Lua hooks (if any) are deferred to a follow-on phase. The LGE _onLoop dispatcher cluster mentioned in the task brief is NOT visible from the FUN_004E20A0 / FUN_004E30A0 / FUN_004B3C50 chain.

actor_cluster_opcode_processing_hypothes: The Actor cluster opcode effects (0x00CA AddActor, 0x00CB RemoveActor, and the 24-opcode multi-case fallthrough at 0x0F / 0xCC..0xE5 covering MoveActor/SetActorPosition/SetActorSpeed/SetActorAppearance/etc.) are NOT applied directly inside FUN_004DC690's actor->vftable[9] call (that slot is no-op per the actor-vtable9-bulk pass). Instead the effect-application happens TWO STEPS LATER: (1) when an Actor cluster s2c packet arrives, FUN_004DC690's per-case body (the 24-case fallthrough, dedicated cases 0xCA/0xCB, or case 7) RE-INTERPRETS the packet payload and WRITES into the actor state directly (the actor map at zone+0x17804..+0x17808 + actor object fields), AND/OR queues a per-actor event into the ring buffer at zone+0x18 / zone+0x14 that FUN_004DAA10 drains; (2) on the NEXT frame tick, FUN_004B3C50 calls FUN_004DAA10 BEFORE FUN_004E30A0/FUN_004E20A0 - FUN_004DAA10 drains the queue and for each entry invokes actor->vtable[8] (offset 0x20) with (event_type-3, payload+0x20, payload+0x18); the actor's own vtable[8] implementation interprets the event_type and applies the position/animation/etc. mutation. The actor-vtable9-bulk pass's mistake was to look at vtable[9] - the correct slot is vtable[8]. A follow-on phase should: (a) survey vtable[8] across the same Actor class set the actor-vtable9-bulk pass surveyed to confirm it is non-empty; (b) trace the QUEUE PRODUCER - find which function writes into zone+0x18 ring buffer with state 1 (ready); the most likely candidate is one of FUN_004DC690's per-case bodies but it could also be in the network-receive callbacks BEFORE the queue dispatch. The opcode-to-event_type mapping is the missing piece: each Actor cluster opcode case in FUN_004DC690 (cases 0x0F, 0xCC, 0xCD, 0xCE, 0xCF, 0xD0, 0xD3-0xE5) probably enqueues an event with event_type = (3 + opcode_subtype) so that FUN_004DAA10 can dispatch to actor->vtable[8] with event_type-3 = opcode_subtype - this would explain why FUN_004DAA10 subtracts 3 before dispatch.

Also emits a thunk_FUN_004E0240(uVar5, 0, 0) periodically (case 4 inner) where uVar5 is a 0-opcode 0-size record built via FUN_004E3910(0, FUN_00445210(0,0)) - likely a no-op keepalive or a special-purpose tick packet.
